claim.summary: Affine indicator kernel: for s disjoint edge pairs with psi_i of support exactly the pair, W their span, W meeting the cut space only in 0, over F containing F_4, identify F[W] with functions on chi in {0,1,2}^s (m_(psi_i)(chi) = omega^(chi_i)) and put x_i = [chi_i = 1], y_i = [chi_i = 2], z_i = x_i + y_i. (a) 1 + q_S, q_S = sum over i in S of m_(psi_i), vanishes exactly where sum_S x_i = sum_S y_i = 1 + |S| (mod 2), with indicator (sum_S x + |S|)(sum_S y + |S|) of degree <= 4. (b) For products P_a = prod_j (1 + q_(S_(a,j))), a <= M, and a nonempty set A, the intersection of c conditions, each an F_2 equation in the one-hot bits or a coordinate condition chi_i = a, together reading u coordinates, with A inside every zero set of P_a, and e = min(c, u): 1_A has degree <= 2e, P_a 1_A g = 0 for all a and g, and for 2e <= K <= D the joint kernel of f -> (R_D(P_a f))_a on degree <= K contains 1_A V_(K-2e), on which g -> R_D(1_A g) has rank >= max(1, h(K - 2e)/s_A). (c) One row S_a per product gives A cut out by 2r forms, r the F_2-rank of the rows, nonempty only if every dependency among them has even length, containing chi = 0 when every |S_a| is odd. (d) Rows S != S' of one product cover Z_(S+S') intersected with {sum_S z = 0}.
claim.assessment: Working proof of (a) by the parity of the counts of each value of chi_i over S and omega^2 = 1 + omega, of (b) by the pointwise product on the dual group, the one-hot monomial expansion, lem:cut-code-classes with W meeting the cut space only in 0 and lem:sparse-weight-survival, of (c) by summing the equations of a dependency, of (d) by c_(S') = c_S + |S + S'|; pending the review of its entry. The parity rule and (b) checked exactly in sector 0 on 208 instances at s <= 8.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: The common killers of pair products have degree set by the rank of the chosen rows and by unions of factors, not by the number of products: the subadditive case of the product of denominators, here through the parity form of each factor's zero set.
significance.next_action: For t >= 2 and M random dense products beyond K/4, a union bound over affine sets of codimension at most K/2 inside every zero set, then whether killers that are not affine indicators exist.

claim.summary: Sector joint kernel sizes: in sector 0 of the pair characters (degree 2k = junta degree k in the one-hot bits), the exact F_2 joint kernel of V_k for s in {6, 7, 8}, k in {2, 3}, t in {2, 3}, M <= 7 (M <= 5 at s = 8), 156 random dense instances with independent rows and 52 coordinate instances: the parity rule held everywhere; of 132 dense instances with M >= 2, 8 had a nonzero joint kernel, none at M >= 4; the hypothesis that no single-factor affine killer of degree <= k means a zero kernel held on 124 of the 125 instances the bare count did not decide and failed on one, s = 7, k = 2, t = 3, M = 2, whose kernel is the indicator of {chi_0 = 0} intersected with {z_1 + z_4 + z_5 + z_6 = 0}, a union cover of two rows of one product. The minimum-weight bound (a nonzero function of junta degree <= k has >= 3^(s-k) nonzeros) forces the kernel to zero on 64 of the 132 dense instances with M >= 2, none of them nonzero.

claim.summary: Pair sector bounds: in lem:pair-occupancy's setting with pi < epsilon, for a nonzero P in the span of the characters of W of support at most e, K + e <= D, with c(k) the rank of f -> R_D(P f) on degree <= k and c_C(k) that rank on the characters of support <= k of a coset C of B + W: (i) c(k) = sum_C c_C(k) (lem:cut-code-sectors with S = (W+B)/B); (ii) 1 <= c_C(k) <= min(n_C(k), 3^s), W meeting B only in 0, so q_W(k) <= c(k) <= min(h(k), 3^s q_W(k)) for k <= K; (iii) the two ratio bounds these give, 3^s q_W(K-d)/q_W(K) and h(K-d)/q_W(K), exceed h(K-d)/h(K) by at least 3^s (1 - eta_W)(1 - eta_occ) and (1 - eta_occ)(1 - q) e^(sK/m), q = K/(2(m-s-K+1)), using that ball ratios B_n'(k-d)/B_n'(k) do not fall when coordinates are removed. (i) and (ii) need only K + e <= D, s <= D and pi < epsilon; (iii) also needs the lemma's hypotheses at levels K-d and K and eta_occ < 1. On the power-growing charged family, for D/2 < s <= D - K and pi <= Delta/8, both factors are N^(Omega(n)), so these two bounds built from c_C >= 1 cannot give the decisive test's yes outcome; a block form combining the counts with the ranks of P inside the sectors is not covered.

claim.summary: Over any field, on a finite product domain X = prod_j A_j (nonempty factors) with base states and one-hot variables x_(j,a) for non-base a (degree = least polynomial degree in them), a nonzero function vanishing on a union of cylinders (partial assignments) has degree at least the transversal number of their coordinate sets; if every coordinate of a least transversal T has a state no cylinder assigns there, the product of those state indicators (each of degree <=1) attains it. On the hole-respecting assignments of the product pigeonhole system, with base state empty, the least degree of a nonzero function vanishing on the supports of monomial errors on distinct holes is the transversal number of their hole sets, which is the least degree of a surviving common killer of 1 when tau<=K and K+e is inert, or D=n with K+e<=n and K<=n-1; for tau>K there is none of degree <=K.

claim.summary: For finitely many module errors vanishing after localization and a protected element surviving there, a product of denominators kills all errors and preserves the element, with additive filtration cost. Fixed linear common-kernel survival descends across finite field extensions without degree increase. Controls: in k[x,y]/(x,y)^2 no annihilator of (x) preserves y; in k[t]/t^(m+1) annihilators of (t) first occur at degree m; in k[u,v]/(u^2,v^2) useful f=u is nilpotent and localization at it is zero; rank-one error data at t distinct evaluation points still require locator degree at least t.
claim.assessment: Working elementary transfer proofs and exact algebraic counterexamples, passed by the sole medium reviewer. Finite-extension scope retained for the motivating use. Support, matrix rank and scalar extension alone give no universal cheap multiplier theorem.

claim.summary: Pair product rank floor: in the charged character window (over F containing F_4, multigraphs included), for s pairwise disjoint edge pairs with psi_i of support exactly the pair, pi the largest number of paired edges at a vertex, a binary t-by-s matrix C, q_j = sum_i C_ji m_(psi_i) and P = prod_(j<=t)(1 + q_j), with K >= 1, K + 2t <= D, pi < epsilon/2, rho = (epsilon - 2pi)/(2(epsilon - pi)), beta = (eK/(rho(m - 2s)))^rho < 1 and eta = (1 + 2 beta^(epsilon - pi))^n - 1, the rank c_P(K) of f -> R_D(P f) on degree <= K satisfies: (a) if C has rank t, c_P(K) >= (1 - eta) B_(m-2t)(K) >= (1 - eta)(1 - 2t/(m - K))^K B_m(K); (b) if s >= K + t, with zeta_C = sum over nonzero lambda in F_2^t of (2K/m)^|lambda^T C|, then for every b with 0 < b < s - K - t + 1, c_P(K) >= (1 - b/(s - K - t + 1))^t (1 - eta - zeta_C - s(K/m)^2/b) B_m(K). P's top part is sum over t-sets T of det(C_T) m_(psi_T) (a binary permanent is a determinant in characteristic two); for each character alpha of a good frame whose touched pairs leave C of rank t and whose psi-valued pairs avoid a pivot set T_0, alpha + psi_(T_0) is the leading class of P m_alpha in an order by support, frame and lex with T_0 first, and these classes are distinct and good; (a) uses one pivot set in every frame.
claim.assessment: Working proof by a leading-term triangularity, a frame-wise good-character union bound adapted from lem:pair-occupancy and a Markov bound on the psi-valued pairs, passed by a fresh-context medium reviewer after it found the first statement false for b >= s - K - t + 1; part (a), the reviewer's fixed-pivot suggestion, verified against the proof. The triangularity checked exactly in the cut-free model on 15 small instances with a zero-determinant control.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.
